newsitem.title: CHINA: Whirlpool sees China sales rising 50-70 pct.
newsitem.headline: Whirlpool sees China sales rising 50-70 pct.

text.p: The U.S. Whirlpool Corp sees business in China growing by 50 to 70 percent a year over the next five years, the Xinhua news agency quoted a senior company official as saying.
China sales were likely to become a major driving force for the company's profit growth, it quoted Matthew Sekellick, who oversees Whirlpool's China business, as saying in an overnight report.
Whirlpool received 90,000 orders for washing machines in China's largest city of Shanghai a week ago, he said as an example of the rapidly growing market.
China's household electrical appliance market could overtake that of North America in the next 10 years, Xinhua quoted Roy Armes, chairman of Whirlpool Greater China Inc, as saying.
Chinese consumers buy 20 million household electrical appliances a year, about 40 percent of Asia's total, Armes said.

Whirlpool has invested $150 million in China since 1994 and set up five joint ventures that manufacture a range of products from air conditioners and microwave ovens to washing machines and refrigerators.
